changes.before: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.after: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December suggests that labor market conditions improved further even as economic growth slowed late last year.

changes.before: Household spending and business fixed investment have been increasing at solid rates in recent months, and the housing sector has improved further; however, net exports have been soft.
changes.after: Household spending and business fixed investment have been increasing at moderate rates in recent months, and the housing sector has improved further; however, net exports have been soft and inventory investment slowed.

changes.before: Overall, taking into account domestic and international developments, the Committee sees the risks to the outlook for both economic activity and the labor market as balanced.

changes.after: The Committee is closely monitoring global economic and financial developments and is assessing their implications for the labor market and inflation, and for the balance of risks to the outlook.

changes.before: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; some survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have edged down.
changes.after: Market-based measures of inflation compensation declined further; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in recent months.

changes.before: Inflation is expected to rise to 2 percent over the medium term
changes.after: Inflation is expected to remain low in the near term, in part because of the further declines in energy prices, but to rise to 2 percent over the medium term

changes.before: The Committee judges that there has been considerable improvement in labor market conditions this year, and it is reasonably confident that inflation will rise, over the medium term, to its 2 percent objective.

A range of recent labor market indicators, including ongoing job gains and declining unemployment, shows further improvement and confirms that underutilization of labor resources has diminished appreciably since early this year.
changes.after: A range of recent labor market indicators, including strong job gains, points to some additional decline in underutilization of labor resources.

parsed.rationale: The Committee held rates after the prior hike, downgraded its growth assessment, dropped the balanced-risks judgment and the 'reasonably confident' inflation language, and flagged global financial developments, signaling a slower pace of tightening. Forward guidance on gradual increases was unchanged, so the shift is moderately dovish rather than a change in direction.

spans.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
Household spending and business fixed investment have been increasing at solid rates in recent months, and the housing sector has improved further; however, net exports have been soft.
Overall, taking into account domestic and international developments, the Committee sees the risks to the outlook for both economic activity and the labor market as balanced.
Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; some survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have edged down.
Inflation is expected to rise to 2 percent over the medium term

The Committee judges that there has been considerable improvement in labor market conditions this year, and it is reasonably confident that inflation will rise, over the medium term, to its 2 percent objective.

A range of recent labor market indicators, including ongoing job gains and declining unemployment, shows further improvement and confirms that underutilization of labor resources has diminished appreciably since early this year.
Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December suggests that labor market conditions improved further even as economic growth slowed late last year.

Household spending and business fixed investment have been increasing at moderate rates in recent months, and the housing sector has improved further; however, net exports have been soft and inventory investment slowed.
The Committee is closely monitoring global economic and financial developments and is assessing their implications for the labor market and inflation, and for the balance of risks to the outlook.
Market-based measures of inflation compensation declined further; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in recent months.
Inflation is expected to remain low in the near term, in part because of the further declines in energy prices, but to rise to 2 percent over the medium term
A range of recent labor market indicators, including strong job gains, points to some additional decline in underutilization of labor resources.
